scope_note: Historical validation of metaspike_score_v0, an internal attention measure, against what the same demand signal did afterwards. It is not evidence about the final creator-opportunity model, which does not exist yet. Read the evidence status before any number.

terms.name: realized_uplift_72h (primary)
terms.rationale: P is the moment of the recommendation; f is the first whole UTC day beginning at or after P; [P] marks a level as it was known at P, from the days its source had published by then. Did demand after the recommendation exceed the game's normal level as it was known when the recommendation was made? Positive: above it. Exactly 0: equal to it. Negative: below it. Never clipped. Seventy-two hours is long enough to make and publish something and short enough that the recommendation is still the reason. For a daily signal that is the next three complete days.

terms.name: movement_24h
terms.rationale: The very next day, against the three-day level the snapshot already knew: did attention keep moving or stall at once?

terms.name: persistence_7d
terms.rationale: A week covers one whole weekly cycle, so a weekday effect cannot pass for persistence.

terms.name: lead_time_days
terms.formula: 1 + smallest k in 0..5 with x[f+k] > x[f+k-1] and x[f+k] >= x[f+k+1] and x[f+k] > baseline_median_28d[P]
terms.rationale: The furthest day inside the week whose following day is also inside it, so a peak is always confirmed by a decline and never assumed at the edge.

parameters.name: hit_threshold
parameters.rationale: Ten percent above the game's own normal level is the smallest uplift treated as more than ordinary day-to-day variation. A stated prior, not a fitted value.

parameters.name: downside_threshold
parameters.rationale: The same distance below normal. Symmetric on purpose.

unavailable.name: future_incomplete
unavailable.formula: any day of the measure's forward window is missing or not yet recorded
unavailable.rationale: A missing day is never filled with zero and never averaged around.

unavailable.name: no_reference
unavailable.formula: the snapshot recorded no baseline, or a baseline of 0
unavailable.rationale: There is nothing to compare the future with.

unavailable.name: not_scored_at_snapshot
unavailable.formula: the game had no score at the snapshot
unavailable.rationale: No recommendation was made, so there is none to hold to account.

strategies.label: MetaSpike score v0
strategies.description: The published rank: attention anomaly and momentum, then confidence, then slug.

strategies.label: Raw popularity
strategies.description: Latest observed daily value, highest first. What a list of big games would say.

strategies.label: Simple lift
strategies.description: The 3-day average over the 28-day baseline median, highest first.

strategies.label: Simple velocity
strategies.description: The 3-day average over the preceding 3 days, highest first.

checks.rationale: Below a month of days or twenty games a result describes those games in that month and nothing else.
A season of days across a hundred games is enough to look for patterns worth testing, not to conclude from.
Half a year, several hundred games and a second, independent demand source, and in addition a held-out period the rules were not chosen on.

evidence.holdout_rationale: This protocol evaluates one period in-sample. It has no held-out period, so it cannot report validated however large the sample is.
evidence.conclusion: Framework only. This sample shows that the backtest runs, that it does not look ahead and that its numbers are reproducible. It is too small to say anything about whether the score predicts demand, and nothing here should be read as evidence for or against it.

leakage_checks.name: source_publication_lag_respected
leakage_checks.description: Every series given to a prediction held no period its source had not yet published at the simulated moment, under that source's publication lag; and no prediction rests on a day later than its source's latest due day.

leakage_checks.name: outcome_window_after_prediction
leakage_checks.description: Every outcome window starts on the first whole day after the simulated moment, and after the newest day the prediction used.

leakage_checks.name: reproduced_after_labelling
leakage_checks.description: After every outcome had been read, each prediction was computed again from scratch and had the identical snapshot id.

leakage_checks.name: unchanged_when_unseen_values_altered
leakage_checks.description: For the first, middle and last day, every value not yet published at that moment was multiplied by 7 and the prediction recomputed: identical. This includes days that had ended but were not yet published.

leakage_checks.name: reference_frozen_at_snapshot
leakage_checks.description: Every label's reference level is the one its snapshot recorded; none was computed from later data.

events.note: Real event backtesting is unavailable: no historical event observations exist. Event Heat is carried in a snapshot when it was available at that moment, is not part of score v0, and is neither evaluated nor tuned here.

limitations: In-sample only: one period, one protocol, no held-out data.

One demand source (Wikimedia daily pageviews). The outcome is measured on the same signal the score is computed from, so it measures whether attention continued, not whether a creator would have gained anything.
Readership of an encyclopedia article is a proxy for demand. It is not views, players, search interest or creator supply.

A value is taken as visible once its source would have published it, under the source's stated publication lag. That lag is a policy figure, not a measured publication time, and a recording made afterwards cannot show values the source later revised.

Recommendations are simulated once a day, at 00:00 UTC. With a one-day lag the day that has just ended is not yet visible, so each recommendation rests on data two days old, and that unseen day is in neither the inputs nor the outcome.
Outcomes on neighbouring days overlap (each uses the next three days), so the observations are not independent and the counts overstate the evidence.
No confidence intervals are reported. With this sample they would imply a precision that does not exist.
Event intelligence took no part. There is no real historical event source, so event_heat_rules_v1 has not been backtested and nothing is claimed for it.
metaspike_score_v0 is an internal attention measure, not the final creator-opportunity score. A result here is about v0 only.
